transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've called us together to go over the middle school civics assessment administration plan before I issue the final version. As you may know, the assessment must be administered during our district's May testing window. The current draft places all registered students in a single administration in the main hall on May 14, using four general proctors. Before I can approve and finalize this plan, I need to follow our standing pre-administration routine and get confirmation from each of you on your respective areas: facilities, enrollment, staffing, and student scheduling. I'd like to go around the table and hear from each of you so we can identify any issues before I give final approval.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a facilities conflict before we proceed. The main hall is actually reserved for a school board meeting on May 14. I confirmed this with facilities earlier this week. The good news is that the library has been cleared for state testing and is set up with 40 individual desks. However, the testing calendar still lists the main hall, which is outdated and needs to be corrected.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag an enrollment issue. I finalized the roster yesterday, and the final enrollment count is 73 students. The cleared library only has a 40-desk capacity, which means we cannot fit all 73 students in a single administration — we'll need two separate administrations. Also, I have not yet updated the enrollment count in the testing portal, so the draft plan's enrollment figure is outdated and needs to be corrected before we finalize.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a staffing issue. Only two of the four listed proctors hold current state-testing proctor certifications. I verified the certificates against the state roster this week. State rules require one certified proctor and one trained monitor in each testing room, but the staffing list still labels all four people only as general proctors. If we move to two separate administrations as Ms. Rivera suggests, we would need at least two certified proctors — one per testing room — and we only have two available. This needs to be corrected before the plan is finalized.
transcript.speaker: A4
